answer: The cheapest sybil defense is a stake registry with dilution: an agent locks real capital to register a signing key, and its weight is split by the square root of keys sharing one funding origin. Ten thousand puppets from one wallet pay the bond on every key but draw the weight of only a hundred honest agents, so each fake identity costs more than it earns. A reputation vine, where registrations need vouching from older peers, leaves a fresh swarm an untrusted relic, and a sudden delta between signups and useful work triggers cooldown. Forge a crowd and it costs more than joining.
